patch_title: Shh... This Won't Hurt a Bit.

systems_changed.change_summary: Every neutral camp is now one of nine named Haunt creature types with its own group/chase/hit behavior, so the camp layer is content, not a timer table. Clear routes, sustain math and camp value must be re-learned per type rather than memorized per spawn.
driving_changes: Haunts: all neutral camps replaced by new creature types (Specimen, Gutter Ghouls, Barrel Mimics, Past Dues, Stage Hands, Crabbage Pots, Festival Spirit, Shrooms, Underhands) with new behaviors — prior clear routes, timings and sustain math no longer transfer
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Farm efficiency becomes a kit question (AoE to hit grouped chasers, regen to survive the damage, disengage if a camp turns) instead of a route question. Kits that must single-target or take chip damage per camp fall behind on income without dying loudly.

systems_changed.change_summary: Some breakables are now Barrel Mimics — smashing jungle crates is no longer guaranteed income and can turn into a fight. The 'free souls on the walk between camps' assumption is gone.
driving_changes: Barrel Mimics: some breakables are now mimics — smashing crates and boxes in the jungle is no longer free souls
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Crate-clearing adds risk to what was a zero-risk income habit, and low-HP clearers get punished for chaining breakables while weak. The payoff skews to kits that can kill a mimic instantly or heal through it.

systems_changed.change_summary: Four off-lane corridors (Theater, Chinatown, Haunted Lot, Plaza) now carry their own content, pulling soul income off the three lanes. The map has more simultaneous farm sites than a five-player team can cover.
driving_changes: Districts: four off-lane corridors added (Theater, Chinatown, Haunted Lot, Plaza) with their own content — souls are no longer concentrated on the three lanes
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Lane static-holding loses value; the team that rotates through corridor content banks more and creates more pick angles. It also means fewer bodies per lane, so ganks and collapses arrive from directions old lane reads don't predict.

systems_changed.change_summary: A high-risk sub-area below the Plaza square where stamina drains on descent and outside sound fades — entry is cheap, exit is not. It pays committed kits and taxes low-mobility or disengage-poor ones.
driving_changes: Sunken Plaza: high-risk sub-area below the Plaza District square; stamina drains as you descend and outside sound fades — taxes low-mobility and disengage-poor kits, pays those who can commit
systems_changed.effect_on_play: It becomes a commitment check: mobile, burst-y kits can farm it and leave, while immobile farmers effectively hand a kill to anyone who follows them down. Stamina drain doubles as a fight-denial tool for whoever arrives first.

systems_changed.change_summary: A vertical Chinatown hotspot whose soul payout rings a map-wide bell, converting a farm route into a broadcast gank target. Income and information are now the same action.
driving_changes: Bell Tower: Chinatown vertical objective; concentrated soul hotspot at the top, but collecting rings the bell map-wide — turns a farm route into a broadcast gank target
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Farming the top is a public commitment, so it wants either a teammate holding the rope or a kit that can escape vertically. It also gives roamers a scheduled convergence point instead of a lucky one.

systems_changed.change_summary: Heavy-Melee-gated breakables pay extra souls, creating a farm lane lanes cannot contest. Heavy-melee access is now a direct income stat, not just a dueling tool.
driving_changes: Tough Crates: breakables requiring a Heavy Melee that pay extra souls — rewards heavy-melee access and gives melee-capable kits a farm lane lanes cannot contest
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Frontline and melee bruisers get a guaranteed income floor while ranged glass kits farm slower off the same map. It rewards putting a body in the jungle rather than in lane, which suits tank/frontline tempo.

systems_changed.change_summary: Golden statues now roll permanent Spirit Resist, Bullet Resist, Ability Range and Move Speed, so the pickup is a permanent-stat draft rather than a heal. Contest value rises for tanks (defensive rolls) and casters (range).
driving_changes: Buff Containers: revamped golden statues now also roll permanent Spirit Resist, Bullet Resist, Ability Range and Move Speed — not just a damage/health pickup, so permanent-buff contests matter for tanks and casters alike
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Contesting containers is now worth a rotation and a fight, and the roll itself creates asymmetry — a Bullet Resist roll changes a duel outcome for the rest of the match. It pushes early skirmishing toward the containers instead of the lanes.

systems_changed.change_summary: Hidden map pickups give a heal in place, cutting forced base returns during lane phase. Lane uptime rises, and chip damage converts into map pressure less reliably.
driving_changes: Healing Snacks: hidden pickups scattered around the map for healing in a pinch — reduces forced base returns during lane phase
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Poke that would have forced a recall now just moves the opponent to a snack, so sustained lane pressure matters more than one big trade. Suits bullies and sustain kits, hurts pure poke.

systems_changed.change_summary: Standing on a vent grants invisibility plus small regen — a reusable stealth tile rather than a hero ability. Gank setup and disengage become map skills available to every kit.
driving_changes: Steam Vents: standing on one grants invisibility and small regen — new gank setup and disengage tool; makes vision and grouped rotations stronger
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Every hero gets a soft escape and an ambush angle, so overextending near a vent is punished and grouped rotations beat solo picks. Vision denial becomes a real cost, favoring teams that travel together.

systems_changed.change_summary: A relocating merchant injects Corrupted items into the economy from ~30 minutes, then roughly every 15 minutes, at a per-match location. A mid/late-game contested point is created on a schedule the map does not advertise.
driving_changes: The Broker: temporary merchant that relocates per match (dark uptown alley, abandoned Chinatown storefront); first stock around 30 minutes, further Corrupted items roughly every 15 minutes after — pulls players to a contested point in the mid/late game
systems_changed.effect_on_play: It gives losing teams a scheduled reason to group and fight, and gives winning teams a place to force a decisive fight — either way the game converges on a known point instead of a PvE race. Corrupted rolls are symmetric, so it's a tempo swing, not a comeback lever.

systems_changed.change_summary: The ritual camp no longer runs on a fixed timer, so pre-timing it from memory fails. Camp planning shifts from schedule knowledge to scouting.
driving_changes: Sinner's Sacrifice: bonus now has variable timings — the ritual is no longer a fixed-timer camp, so pre-timing it is harder
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Small, but it removes another memorized timer, which is the patch's recurring theme: you have to look at the map instead of the clock.

systems_changed.change_summary: Casting fires on button press instead of the next input window — every hero gains a frame of responsiveness on casts, cancels and parries.
driving_changes: Ability/item cast: fires the instant the button is pressed instead of on the next input window — reaction speed, cancels and clutch parries get tighter for every hero
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Higher-execution play is rewarded: combos land more reliably and clutch parries become a real skill expression. This raises the ceiling on burst and reaction-based kits without changing any number.

systems_changed.change_summary: Parrying an objective no longer resets the parry cooldown, deleting the free defensive reset before a dive. Committing under a Guardian now carries an un-refunded cooldown.
driving_changes: Parry: successfully parrying objectives no longer resets Parry cooldown — objective-parry stops being a free defensive reset before a fight
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Objective dives and defenses are one-shot decisions: tanks with bullet resist can still commit under a Guardian, but nobody gets a second parry for free. Slightly favors the attacker who forces the parry early.

systems_changed.change_summary: Walkers stop firing fireballs after death, so killing one removes the zone immediately rather than after the corpse clears.
driving_changes: Walkers: no longer keep firing fireballs after dying — diving a Walker you just killed is now safe
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Siege sequences get cleaner — kill the Walker, then commit into the space behind it without eating posthumous chip. Small, but it rewards fast conversion after a pick instead of waiting out the corpse.

systems_changed.change_summary: Lanes renamed Broadway (blue), Greenwich (green), York (yellow) with a visual rework — old lane vocabulary and its muscle memory are dated.
driving_changes: Lanes: renamed Broadway (blue), Greenwich (green), York (yellow) — callouts change with the visual rework; treat old lane knowledge as dated
systems_changed.effect_on_play: A short-term coordination tax on every team, and a real edge for stacks that relearn callouts fast. No economic effect beyond early-patch confusion.

systems_changed.change_summary: Six new heroes ship two per week on a voted order, with voting moved to the Pregame lobby (winning team's votes double) and play earning priority tokens; Street Brawl grants a corrupted item after the Round 5 draft.
driving_changes: Hero releases: six new heroes, two per week on Tue/Fri 2:00pm PT, first release Oct 2, order decided by vote; voting moved to the Pregame lobby with the winning team's votes counting double, and play earns priority tokens
Street Brawl: corrupted item granted after the Round 5 item draft
systems_changed.effect_on_play: A staggered rollout means the roster is unstable week to week, so archetype reads are provisional and day-one pick/win data is noise. Corrupted items enter Brawl at the same mid-point they enter the main mode, keeping that mode's power curve aligned.

tempo_shift.why: Souls spread across four off-lane corridors, Heavy-Melee Tough Crates and contested Buff Containers reward early rotations and map presence over lane farming, and Healing Snacks plus Steam Vents cut the cost of staying out. The Broker's ~30-minute stock is the counterweight that can stall a game, but the bell-broadcast and container fights resolve earlier.

archetype_effects.why: Heavy-Melee Tough Crates give a guaranteed uncontestable soul route, harder Haunt camps reward sustain stacks, and Buff Container's permanent Bullet/Spirit Resist rolls are tank stats.
Four off-lane corridors, Steam Vent invisibility and Bell Tower's broadcast gank target hand roamers scheduled pick angles they didn't have on three lanes.
Healing Snacks remove forced base returns during lane phase, so converted lane pressure sticks instead of resetting on a recall.
Bell Tower rings map-wide and Buff Container contests are permanent-stat fights, giving initiators fixed points to force engagements on.
Grouped rotations beat Steam Vent solos and Healing Snacks supplement in-fight sustain, both favoring a body that enables the group.
Walker fireballs stopping on death and instant casts help conversion, but Healing Snacks blunt the chip damage that poke relies on — roughly a wash.
Buff Container's Ability Range roll helps, but its permanent Spirit Resist roll gives opponents a stacking answer to spirit damage.
Bullet Resist and Move Speed rolls on contested containers cut both ways, and The Broker's per-match Corrupted stock adds variance rather than a guaranteed spike.
Casts now fire on button press rather than the next input window, tightening combo execution, and Ability Range is a permanent container roll.
Souls moving off the lanes into corridors means sidelane pressure converts to less income, and shared map objectives pull the pusher's team elsewhere.
Corridor souls, contested containers and bell-broadcast fights bank tempo before a late spike; The Broker at ~30 minutes is the only scheduled late-game bailout.

systems.intent_read: Valve is deleting route memorization: souls move off the three lanes into corridors, sub-areas and behavior-varied Haunt camps, so income comes from reading the map and fitting a kit to the content rather than knowing timers. The Broker and Bell Tower exist to convert farming into announced, contested fights, so games resolve on map pressure instead of a PvE race — and the push is deliberately toward tempo, at the cost of late-scaling identities.

items.summary: A new late-game gold sink rather than a build slot: you trade an item you already own for a stronger-with-a-downside version, so it changes nothing about early build paths and only taxes the 25-40 minute gold decision. Because every Corrupted item in a lobby rolls the same negative attributes (small magnitude variance), the downside is public information — both teams know exactly which stat is degraded, so the edge goes to whoever's build cares least about that roll, not to whoever bought it first. Whether it is net strong or net weak is unclear (no KB entry, no numbers), so treat this as a low-confidence rework read.
items.build_shift: The exchange doesn't move components or add a slot; it competes with sixth-slot completion and counter-item purchases, and it rewards banking souls for the ~30-minute Broker stock — an anti-tempo habit in a patch that otherwise pays you to spend and rotate.

notable_item_stories: Corrupted Items are a win-more lever: an ahead team converts surplus souls into stacked corrupted upgrades every ~15 minutes, so despite the Broker being a scheduled group-and-fight point for losing teams, the economy gap widens if the ahead team wins that fight.

Since the negative roll is identical for everyone and visible, corrupted items turn into an exploit map — you know which stat your opponents lost and can build or fight into that hole, which favors teams that actually check the roll over teams that just take the upgrade.

The Broker relocates per match and isn't advertised on the map, so the first corrupt is a scouting check; in uncoordinated lobbies the tempo lost hunting the merchant likely exceeds the item's value, which quietly favors stacks.

indirect_reasons: Grouped, chasing Haunt camps are the biggest income route now and his burn AoE clears them without extra items.
Buff Containers roll permanent Spirit Resist, a match-long answer to burn/spirit damage that he cannot strip.
Containers also roll Ability Range and Move Speed, which feeds the Dashfernus spirit line more than the gun line.
build_changes: Skip Tough Crates entirely — he has no heavy-melee route; farm grouped camps instead.
In lobbies that stack Bullet/Spirit Resist container rolls, lean on the gun/burn build over pure spirit.
heroes.one_liner: Camps and containers both like him; his two builds don't change.

indirect_reasons: Storm Cloud/Static Charge is still the fastest clear of the new behavior-varied Haunt camps — and camp income is now the main soul route.
Bell Tower and Sunken Plaza force the grouped hub fights his AoE farms best.
The tempo push still ends games before a behind Seven recovers, so this rewards the lead, not the comeback.
build_changes: Keep the Monster Rounds/Cultist Sacrifice farm opener; corridor camps replace lane static-holding.
Only rope up to Bell Tower with a teammate holding the rope — the bell is a map-wide gank call.
heroes.one_liner: Fastest camp clearer in the game, and camps are now where souls live.

indirect_reasons: Steam Vents hand every roamer free invisibility, adding approach angles against a low-HP flyer with one escape.
Four off-lane districts thin the bodies in lane, so dives arrive from directions max-range poke cannot pre-aim.
Silver's Weighted Bola and the air-drag slow are unchanged, so the flyer ceiling stays where it was.
build_changes: Keep Counterspell as the mandatory anti-dive slot; nothing here justifies dropping it.
Farm from roofs as before, but do not solo the Bell Tower top.
heroes.one_liner: More high ground, more hiding spots — and more things that can ground her.

indirect_reasons: Buff Containers now roll permanent Bullet/Spirit Resist — frontline stats her regen shell wants for free.
Harder Haunt camps reward her Extra Regen/Mystic Regeneration stack; Tough Crates stay closed to her without a heavy-melee commitment.
Lash and other divers gain from Steam Vents and corridors, and she is still their food.
build_changes: Regen first stays correct — camp chip damage is higher than last patch.
Contest Buff Containers; a Bullet Resist roll is worth more to her than any damage roll.
heroes.one_liner: Tankier from container rolls, still dies to the same dive heroes.

indirect_reasons: His melee core gives a cheap Heavy Melee, the only key to Tough Crates (58 souls each) — an income lane ranged kits cannot contest.
Harder Haunt camps reward his Siphon/melee-lifesteal sustain on the farm route.
Parry no longer resets on objectives: dives on him are one-shot, but his own Guardian-dive loses the free second parry.
build_changes: Insert a Tough-Crate sweep between camp respawns; his heavy melee makes it free souls.
Keep the Close Quarters/Monster Rounds opener — it is the same spike as before.
heroes.one_liner: Heavy melee is now a farm stat, and he owns that route.
Nothing in this patch touches her; still a fire-rate gun carry in a roam meta.

indirect_reasons: Turrets clear the new grouped, chasing Haunt camps without leaving cover.
The objective-parry change punishes dives into her wall/turret zone under a Guardian.
Fights spread across four corridors dilute her static-zone value relative to a three-lane map.
build_changes: Prioritize turret placement on Sunken Plaza and Bell Tower approaches over lane siege.
heroes.one_liner: Her turrets farm the new camps; just stop sieging empty lanes.

indirect_reasons: Four off-lane districts and Steam-Vent invisibility add fresh Kinetic Carbine pick angles off the lanes.
Barrel Mimics make crate-chaining risky for the low-HP clearers she picks on.
build_changes: Set picks from Steam Vents and corridors instead of lane brushes; carbine sniper core unchanged.
heroes.one_liner: The map finally has hiding spots for her carbine picks.

indirect_reasons: Telegraphed Bell Tower and Sunken Plaza fights hand Singularity clean setup windows on grouped teams.
His worst matchups (Billy, Mo & Krill, Abrams) are also up — the frontline archetype rose with him.
build_changes: Payoff stays Refresher/Unstoppable double-ult; spend it on hub contests, not lane.
heroes.one_liner: Grouped fights at objectives are exactly where his ult wins games.

indirect_reasons: Harder, behavior-varied Haunt camps raise the value of dome sustain on the farm route.
Bell Tower and Sunken Plaza make Frozen Shelter a zone tool at forced objective fights.
Healing Snacks cut the number of forced returns he used to heal teammates through.
build_changes: Save the dome for the Bell Tower/Plaza contest; snacks cover the between-camp healing.
heroes.one_liner: His dome is now worth more at objectives than in lane.

indirect_reasons: Corridors plus Steam Vents boost the Smoke Bomb roamer line; the farm-carry line gets nothing from Tough Crates.
Permanent Bullet Resist rolls on Buff Containers blunt gun damage for the rest of the match.
Barrel Mimics punish chaining crates at low HP on a squishy frame.
build_changes: Play vent ambushes on isolated corridor farmers instead of static camp farming.
Never chain breakables while low — a mimic turns a routine clear into a death.
heroes.one_liner: Roam build gains, farm build loses; nothing touches her T4 problem.

indirect_reasons: Four off-lane corridors plus Steam Vent invisibility expand her roam routes beyond the old lanes.
Bell Tower's top payout rings map-wide, which is a scheduled gank spot for a lasso pick.
build_changes: Pre-place bounce-pad exits near the Bell Tower rope before roping; lasso the farmer, not the escort.
heroes.one_liner: More routes and a broadcast target — her kind of map.

indirect_reasons: A single-target hook converts nothing on a spread-out corridor farm route — there is no lane body to punish.
Paradox keeps the roamer slot and the new districts and Steam Vents give her pick angles a hook cannot match.
Steam Vents give every target a free disengage his combo cannot chase.
build_changes: Hook off corridor chokepoints and camp entrances instead of lane.
heroes.one_liner: Hooks still land, but nothing in the new economy punishes a farm route.

indirect_reasons: Districts and Steam Vent invisibility sharpen the tempo roam the no-comeback economy already rewards.
Cat form still cannot Heavy Melee, so Tough Crates stay closed — her income must come from kills and corridors.
The frontline archetype rose, giving her more bodies she cannot burst (Abrams, Rat King).
build_changes: Lean kills and off-map souls; ignore Corrupted items, they are a late gold sink she should not bank for.
heroes.one_liner: Better roam angles, same locked-out crate route.

indirect_reasons: Steam Vents give roamers free invisibility against a sub-50%-WR immobile flyer.
Healing Snacks blunt the chip damage his poke converts into lane leads.
Air-drag slow and Silver's Weighted Bola are unchanged, and neither camp routes nor crates suit him.
heroes.one_liner: Poke carries keep losing value; the map keeps giving divers more ways in.

indirect_reasons: Sustained frontline is what harder Haunt camps and contested Buff Containers reward.
Objective parries no longer reset, so his Guardian-dive chain is now one-shot.
Ranged poke he cannot close on still beats him, and that is unchanged.
build_changes: Frontline the Buff Container contests; a Bullet Resist roll compounds with his T3.
heroes.one_liner: Default front line for a patch that pays for standing in camps.

indirect_reasons: Harder camps reward his regen stack, and the rising frontline feeds current-HP Serrated Knives.
Steam Vents hand divers a free approach on a hero who needs regen ramp time before he is unkillable.
heroes.one_liner: Anti-tank is still the right job; the camp damage just helps him ramp.

indirect_reasons: Healing Snacks plus spread corridors reduce the value of a dedicated healer who wants the team grouped.
Districts pull her team apart, so a single tether covers less of the map than on three lanes.
Her frontline partners (Abrams, Billy) are up, which is the one thing going her way.
build_changes: Tether to a frontline bruiser sweeping corridors rather than a lane partner.
heroes.one_liner: Still the best peel in the game, but the map now punishes grouping less.

indirect_reasons: Steam Vents give every hero the invis-engage he pays Shadow Weave for, flattening his one unique tool.
Tempo still ends games before his late gun spike, and no item or system route slows that.
build_changes: Shadow Weave stays the engage shell, but it no longer buys exclusivity.
heroes.one_liner: Everyone gets a free invis now; his late spike still arrives too late.

direct_reasons: Flying Strike now creates paths against solid targets (turrets, Shrines, objectives) — objective-adjacent ults stop whiffing and she gets a second mobility vector.
indirect_reasons: Her punch AoE remains the fastest clear of the grouped, behavior-varied Haunt camps.
Parry no longer resets on objectives, so her Shrine/Walker dive is one-shot — plan the exit before committing.
build_changes: Use Flying Strike off a Walker or Guardian to path out, not only to engage.
heroes.one_liner: Free pathing off objectives plus the best camp clear: closest thing to S.

indirect_reasons: Districts and Steam Vents extend his dive routes beyond the three lanes.
Bell Tower and Sunken Plaza concentrate teams into exactly his Ground Strike setup.
The objective-parry change removes the free defensive reset from the fights he starts.
build_changes: Rotate corridors between stomps — roam income replaces lane pressure.
heroes.one_liner: More places to dive from, same stomp.

indirect_reasons: Bell Tower's spread vaults and four corridors suit Goo Ball traversal and escapes.
Harder camps reward Cube sustain, and forced hub fights raise Cube rescue value.
build_changes: Hold Cube for the Buff Container or Bell Tower contest, not lane trades.
heroes.one_liner: Cube rescue is worth more when fights are scheduled at objectives.

indirect_reasons: The late-scaler profile stays penalized: corridor income and forced container fights bank tempo before Affliction comes online.
Steam Vents give every hero the ambush value his cloak used to monopolize.
build_changes: Farm corridors with Monster Rounds/Cultist Sacrifice; skip crate chains he cannot survive.
heroes.one_liner: Same bad fit for the economy, one more way to be found out.

indirect_reasons: Split-push loses its payoff — souls moved off the lanes into corridors and shared objectives, so sidelane pressure converts to less income.
Steam Vent invisibility hands roamers a free approach on his map-play.
build_changes: Farm corridors instead of shoving a lane; Djinn's Mark picks isolated camp clearers.
heroes.one_liner: The patch deleted lane-pushing as an income strategy.

indirect_reasons: Buff Containers roll permanent Bullet Resist, a match-long tax on a pure-gun carry.
Barrel Mimics punish close-range crate-chaining while low on a hero with no disengage.
build_changes: Nothing to swap; the pure-gun pivot is worse into resist rolls, not better.
heroes.one_liner: Every container roll of Bullet Resist is a small loss for her.
Nothing here changes a hero who wins by stealing someone else's kit.

indirect_reasons: Grouped Haunt camps suit her AoE clear, and the new districts give her dive routes.
The tank/frontline archetype rose, and tanks are her worst matchups.
build_changes: Dive corridor farmers between camps; skip crates, she has no heavy-melee route.
heroes.one_liner: The camps love her; the tanks she cannot kill got better.

indirect_reasons: Steam Vents and the new hiding spots fit his stealth-reveal roam exactly.
Heavy-Melee Tough Crates give his melee core the same uncontestable soul lane the tanks got.
The frontline archetype rose, though so did his counters Dynamo and Mo & Krill.
build_changes: Sweep Tough Crates between roams; Stalker stays the first buy.
heroes.one_liner: Melee bruiser with a private income lane and free hiding spots.

direct_reasons: Graves' gun now destroys his traps, turning a C-tier pick into a direct counter into his zoning.
indirect_reasons: Buff Containers' permanent Bullet Resist roll taxes a gun-bruiser carry for the whole match.
Spread corridors and Steam Vents add flank angles on a slow tanky gunner.
build_changes: Against a Graves, hold traps for fight setup instead of pre-placing them as lane vision.
heroes.one_liner: Trap zoning now has a hero who deletes traps, and he is popular.

indirect_reasons: Harder, behavior-varied Haunt camps and longer PvE routes feed his Spirit Lifesteal/Healing Booster stack.
Buff Containers' Bullet/Spirit Resist rolls are frontline stats he gets for contesting.
build_changes: Contest containers; keep the High-Velocity Rounds/Opening Rounds weapon start.
heroes.one_liner: Camp damage went up; his sustain stack went up with it.

indirect_reasons: Healing Snacks let her lane pressure stick instead of resetting on an opponent's recall.
Lane-adjacent crate routes from ~2:30 keep the tempo lead she builds in lane.
build_changes: Convert the lane win into corridor crate routes rather than a sidelane shove.
heroes.one_liner: Wins lane, and the new map pays lane winners immediately.

indirect_reasons: Bell Tower's single rope and ~280-soul payout give Doorway a real kidnap play on the top platform.
The dive archetype is up (Yamato, Lash, Holliday) and still reaches him before Cart/Doorway set up.
build_changes: Pre-place the door at the Bell Tower base before roping up.
heroes.one_liner: Bell Tower is a kidnap setup with his name on it.

indirect_reasons: Harder Haunt camps and sustained presence reward the frontline archetype he lives in.
The front-line slot still reads Mo & Krill, and ranged corridor clear beats his all-in.
heroes.one_liner: Frontline patch, but he is still the second-best front line.

direct_reasons: Her gun now destroys Venator's traps, making her a genuine counter-pick into a 40%-pick-rate A-tier hero.
indirect_reasons: Split-push and late-scaling both got worse: souls moved into corridors and shared objectives, away from the sidelanes she pressed.
Barrel Mimics punish a low-HP, two-stamina carry chaining breakables.
build_changes: Draft her into Venator specifically; skip risky crate chains while low.
Corrupted items at ~30 minutes are her only realistic late power spike — bank for the Broker.
heroes.one_liner: Finally a reason to pick her: she deletes Venator's traps.

indirect_reasons: His lane-bully pressure now converts into lane-adjacent crate routes and Healing Snacks.
The objective-parry change trims his T3-bullet-resist Guardian dive chain to one shot.
Frontline archetype up and his spirit core untouched.
build_changes: Dive Guardians as a one-shot decision; there is no free second parry.
heroes.one_liner: Still a lane bully, but his free Guardian dive is gone.

indirect_reasons: Harder camps raise the value of a percent-max-HP heal on the farm route.
Healing Snacks cheapen the dedicated healing he sells, and the tank partners who benefit are up.
build_changes: Shadow a frontline bruiser through corridors rather than sitting in a lane.
heroes.one_liner: Sustain matters more, but snacks do part of his job for free.

indirect_reasons: Frontline tempo and forced hub fights suit her gun-tank shell, and Weighted Bola still grounds flyers.
Permanent Bullet Resist container rolls compound her tank side.
She has no heavy-melee crate route, so the patch's best soul lane is closed to her.
build_changes: Play the Bell Tower/Plaza contest and container fights, not the crate sweep.
heroes.one_liner: Anti-air police in a flyer-heavy meta; the snapshot WR says she is over-picked.

indirect_reasons: Flyer tax is intact (air-drag slow, Weighted Bola) while fights concentrate at the vertical Bell Tower.
Late-scaling burst is exactly the profile a tempo patch punishes; Barrel Mimics punish squishy clearers too.
build_changes: Witchmail stays the anti-slow answer; do not rope up alone.
heroes.one_liner: Flying late scaler in a grounded, early-fight patch.

indirect_reasons: His 116 heavy-melee open still cracks Tough Crates for guaranteed ~58 souls each — an uncontestable income route.
Scrap Grenade AoE clears the grouped, chasing Haunt camps and the corridors between them.
Sunken Plaza and Bell Tower force the grouped fights his banner ult was built for.
build_changes: Open the same heavy-melee/HP line and sweep crates before the first camp.
heroes.one_liner: The map was rebuilt around heavy melee, camp AoE and forced fights — his kit.

indirect_reasons: Her melee-regen stack still clears Tough Crates and grouped Haunt camps, the two new income routes.
Grounded bruisers gain from the air-drag slow, and forced hub fights suit her AoE hex and silence.
The 10-14 barrier/resist cuts are unchanged — this patch adds fit, not power.
build_changes: Buy Healing Booster/Spirit Resilience earlier and stop counting on out-tanking focus.
heroes.one_liner: The new map suits her kit; the barrier nerf still does not.

indirect_reasons: Telegraphed Bell Tower and Sunken Plaza fights reward his Bishop/Rook zone control.
The dive archetype is up (Yamato, Lash, Holliday) and still lands before his zones are placed.
build_changes: Set zones on the Bell Tower rope and container spawns, not lanes.
heroes.one_liner: Scheduled fights help him; the heroes that skip his zones are still strong.

indirect_reasons: Spirit AoE marks suit the grouped, chasing Haunt camps that now carry the income.
Bell Tower and Plaza reward mark-then-dive on stacked teams.
The flyer tax is intact and Barrel Mimics punish a 730-HP commit.
build_changes: Farm grouped camps, not crates; keep High-Velocity Rounds as the only weapon staple.
heroes.one_liner: His mark burst likes stacked camps; the air tax still eats him.

indirect_reasons: A 116 heavy-melee open lets her farm Tough Crates and grouped camps like a frontline.
Buff Container and Bell Tower contests are where her silence zone decides the fight.
Steam Vents give dive assassins a free approach on a 710-HP caster with no escape.
build_changes: Spirit plus cooldown only — the High-Velocity Rounds gun line sits at ~28% WR.
heroes.one_liner: Her kit was quietly built for the new map, if she survives the dive.

direct_reasons: New hero shipping in the staggered six-hero rollout; the notes carry no kit, only that she won the release vote.
indirect_reasons: Two heroes per week means her day-one pick and win data is novelty noise, not a read.
heroes.one_liner: No kit in the notes — treat any Harrow take as provisional.

synthesis.size_why: Not a numbers patch: the neutral layer is rebuilt as nine behavior-varied Haunt types, four off-lane districts and sub-areas (Sunken Plaza, Bell Tower) re-price where souls come from, and Barrel Mimics/Steam Vents/Healing Snacks change how farm, vision and disengage work. Zero hero balance numbers means every tier movement is inferred from systems, not tuning.
synthesis.headline: Souls moved off the lanes into corridors, camps and announced hub fights — kits that clear grouped camps and heavy-melee crates bank first, single-target lane bullies and split pushers starve.

meta_thesis.previous: With memorized routes dead, souls come from behavior-varied Haunts, contested Soul Bags, permanent-stat Buff Containers and earlier district objectives, so tempo, fast-clear kits and sustained frontlines carry while late scalers and split pushers fall off.
meta_thesis.new: Same economy, wider map: souls now sit in four off-lane corridors plus sub-areas that a five-man team cannot cover, so income is a coverage question answered by AoE camp clear and heavy-melee crate access, and fights get scheduled at hubs (Bell Tower bell, container contests, ~30-minute Broker) instead of picked in lanes.
meta_thesis.why: The Haunt/container/Broker economy from Paint the Town is extended, not replaced — districts, Bell Tower, Sunken Plaza and Tough Crates were already priced into the KB thesis, so the genuinely new levers are Haunt creature behavior, Barrel Mimics, Steam Vents, Healing Snacks, instant casts and the confirmed Broker cadence.

winners.why: Heavy-melee open cracks Tough Crates for guaranteed souls, Scrap Grenade clears grouped chasing Haunts, and Sunken Plaza/Bell Tower force the stacked fights his ult wants — he is the patch's shape in one kit.
Flying Strike pathing off solid objectives plus the best punch-AoE camp clear makes her the closest thing to S; the lost objective-parry reset only trims her Shrine dive to one shot.
Her gun now destroys Venator's traps, converting an unplayed C-tier into a draftable counter into a ~40%-pick A-tier — the single largest delta any one line in the notes creates.
Melee core gives him the same uncontestable Tough Crate income lane the tanks got, and Steam Vents plus new hiding spots are his stealth-reveal roam with better geometry.
Four corridors and vent invisibility multiply her roam routes, and Bell Tower's map-wide payout is a scheduled lasso target she can pre-plan around.

losers.why: Graves deletes his pre-placed traps, and Bullet Resist container rolls tax a slow gun-bruiser for the full match — A to B on one hero matchup plus one map system.
Sidelane shoving converts to less income now that souls live in corridors and shared objectives; the strategy he was drafted for is the one the map deleted.
Steam Vents hand every hero the invis-engage he pays Shadow Weave for, so his one exclusivity is gone while the tempo clock that kills his late spike is unchanged.
A single-target hook converts nothing on spread corridor farm, Steam Vents give targets a free disengage his combo cannot chase, and Paradox still owns the roamer slot.
Healing Snacks blunt the poke he converts into lane leads and vents hand divers an approach onto a sub-50% immobile flyer; no camp or crate route suits him either.

non_obvious_calls.claim: The headline hero change is a Venator nerf filed under Graves.
non_obvious_calls.why: The line reads as a Graves buff, but its only real effect is deleting trap zoning from a 40%-pick A-tier, which is the largest single-hero swing in a patch with no balance numbers.

non_obvious_calls.claim: Most of the 'new map' was already priced into the KB, so the real new information is smaller than 33 changes implies.
non_obvious_calls.why: Districts, Bell Tower, Sunken Plaza, Tough Crates and the Broker all appear in the pre-patch thesis; the genuinely new inputs are Haunt creature behavior, Barrel Mimics, Steam Vents, Healing Snacks and instant casts.

non_obvious_calls.claim: Barrel Mimics convert crate-chaining from a tempo route into a sustain check, and it hits squishy gun carries hardest.
non_obvious_calls.why: Smashing breakables now risks a fight, so low-HP, no-disengage clearers (Vyper, Graves, Celeste) eat the tax while melee bruisers heal through it — the opposite of the 'free souls on the walk' habit.

non_obvious_calls.claim: Cast-on-press is a silent buff to high-execution combo and parry kits that win rates will not show for a week.
non_obvious_calls.why: Casts firing on the input rather than the next window tightens combos and clutch parries for Yamato, Lash and Paradox without touching a number, so it reads as player skill until the sample stabilizes.

uncertainties: Haunt soul values and clear difficulty are still unstated, so which of the nine camp types is actually worth farming is discovery, not analysis.
Corrupted item power is unquantified, and banking souls for a ~30-minute Broker stock is an anti-tempo habit in a patch that otherwise pays you to spend and rotate.
Six heroes on a voted Tue/Fri rollout make day-one pick and win rates noise for the first two weeks.
The Graves snapshot (56.5% WR / 40.9% PR) still contradicts the KB (48.5% / 21%) and I cannot resolve which is current.
Whether a wider map plus the Broker actually lengthens games past 30 minutes or tempo still closes lobbies first — the two forces point opposite ways.
what_to_watch: Per-Haunt-type clear times and souls banked: if one or two types dominate, farm routes re-converge and the 'no memorization' intent fails.
Average game length and the share of games reaching the ~30-minute Broker window — the cleanest test of tempo versus stall.
Buff Container contest rate, especially Bullet Resist and Move Speed rolls, since those permanently skew duels.
Steam Vent usage in kill participation: if vent ganks spike, grouping discipline becomes the skill gap and solo picks (Bebop, Grey Talon) fall further.
Rat King's win rate against his pick rate — an A-to-S jump this fast usually needs the data to confirm it is not just novelty.
Whether Venator's pick rate collapses specifically into Graves lobbies, confirming the counter-pick read rather than a general decline.

verdicts.one_liner: Graves is now a popular hard counter to his traps; drop from A to B.
verdicts.direct: Graves' gun destroys his pre-placed traps, so trap zoning — his main lane tool — is deleted in any lobby with a Graves (now a ~40% pick).
verdicts.indirect: Permanent Bullet Resist container rolls tax a gun-bruiser for the whole match, and spread corridors plus Steam Vents open flank angles on a slow tanky gunner.
build_adjustments: Against Graves, hold traps for fight setup instead of pre-placing them as lane vision.

verdicts.one_liner: Roam build gains from vents and corridors; farm build gains nothing.
verdicts.indirect: Steam Vents and corridors feed the Smoke Bomb roamer line, but permanent Bullet Resist container rolls blunt gun damage and Barrel Mimics punish crate-chaining on her squishy frame.
build_adjustments: Play vent ambushes on isolated corridor farmers instead of static camp farming.
Never chain breakables at low HP — a mimic turns a routine clear into a death.

verdicts.one_liner: Untouched by the patch; still a fire-rate gun carry in a roam meta.
Vents give everyone his Shadow Weave engage, and he still spikes too late.
verdicts.indirect: Steam Vents hand every hero the invis-engage he pays Shadow Weave for, so his one exclusivity is gone — and the tempo clock that kills his late gun spike is unchanged.
build_adjustments: Shadow Weave stays the engage shell, but it no longer buys exclusivity.

verdicts.one_liner: Harder camps feed his regen ramp; the tank front line he shreds rose.
verdicts.indirect: Harder camp damage rewards his regen stack, and the rising frontline gives current-HP Serrated Knives more targets — though Steam Vents give divers a free approach before he ramps.

verdicts.one_liner: Free pathing off objectives plus the best camp clear: closest thing to S.
verdicts.direct: Flying Strike now creates paths against solid targets (turrets, Shrines, objectives), so objective-adjacent ults stop whiffing; parry no longer resets on objectives, making a Shrine dive one-shot.
verdicts.indirect: Her punch AoE is still the fastest clear of the grouped, behavior-varied Haunt camps, which is where souls now live.
build_adjustments: Use Flying Strike off a Walker or Guardian to path out, not only to engage.
Plan the Shrine/Walker dive exit before committing — no parry reset to bail you out.

verdicts.one_liner: Camps and new districts love her; the tanks she cannot kill also got better.
verdicts.indirect: Grouped Haunt camps suit her AoE clear and the new off-lane districts give her dive routes, but the frontline archetype rose and tanks are her worst matchups.
build_adjustments: Dive corridor farmers between camps; skip Tough Crates, she has no heavy-melee route.

verdicts.one_liner: Four corridors and vent invisibility give her carbine real hiding spots.
verdicts.indirect: Steam-Vent invisibility and off-lane corridors add fresh Kinetic Carbine pick angles, and Barrel Mimics make crate-chaining lethal for the low-HP clearers she picks on.
build_adjustments: Set picks from Steam Vents and corridors instead of lane brushes.

verdicts.one_liner: The patch deleted lane-shoving as an income strategy; his whole plan was that.
verdicts.indirect: Souls moved off the lanes into corridors and shared objectives, so his split-push pressure converts to less income, and Steam Vents hand roamers a free approach on his map-play.
build_adjustments: If you play him, farm corridors instead of shoving a lane and pick isolated camp clearers with Djinn's Mark.

verdicts.one_liner: Camps and containers both like him; neither build changes.
verdicts.indirect: Grouped, chasing Haunt camps are the main income route and his burn AoE clears them itemless, while Buff Containers' permanent Spirit Resist is a match-long answer he cannot strip.
build_adjustments: Skip Tough Crates entirely — farm grouped camps instead.
In lobbies stacking Spirit Resist rolls, lean on the gun/burn build over pure spirit.

verdicts.one_liner: More roam routes and a map-wide announced target: her kind of map.
verdicts.indirect: Four off-lane corridors plus vent invisibility expand her roam routes, and Bell Tower's top payout is a scheduled gank spot for a lasso pick.
build_adjustments: Pre-place bounce-pad exits near the Bell Tower rope before roping; lasso the farmer, not the escort.

verdicts.one_liner: Melee bruiser with a private income lane and free hiding spots.
verdicts.indirect: Heavy-Melee Tough Crates give his melee core the same uncontestable soul lane the tanks got, and Steam Vents plus new hiding spots fit his stealth-reveal roam — though his counters Dynamo and Mo & Krill also rose.
build_adjustments: Sweep Tough Crates between roams; Stalker stays the first buy.

verdicts.one_liner: Frontline patch helps, but he is still the second-best front line.
verdicts.indirect: Harder camps reward the sustained frontline archetype he lives in, but the slot still reads Mo & Krill and rising anti-tank Shiv is his worst lane.
